evals.name: revert-single-bad-commit-on-shared-main
evals.prompt: Commit `a1b2c3d` added a new rate-limiter to `src/api/middleware.ts`. It is now rejecting legitimate traffic in production. The branch `main` is shared by the whole team and several other commits have landed after `a1b2c3d`. How do I undo `a1b2c3d` safely?

assertions.text: The response recommends `git revert a1b2c3d` rather than `git reset --hard`
The response does NOT recommend force-pushing or rewriting history on the shared `main` branch
The response instructs me to reproduce or confirm the breakage before reverting
The response instructs me to verify that the revert actually fixes the issue

evals.name: revert-merge-commit-safely
evals.prompt: Merge commit `m4n5o6p` merged branch `feature/auth-v2` into `main`. After the merge, the login flow broke for users with uppercase emails. We need to undo the merge safely on `main` while keeping `feature/auth-v2` alive so the team can fix it there. What is the exact command and process?

assertions.text: The response uses `git revert -m 1 m4n5o6p` to revert the merge commit
The response preserves the `feature/auth-v2` branch and does not delete or rewrite it
The response does not use `git reset --hard` on `main`
The response does not force-push to the shared `main` branch
The response includes verifying that login works after the revert
